# AGENTS.md

A Node-RED node package for agentic workflows (`@tbrandenburg/node-red-agents`
-- `agent`, `agent-server`, `gh`) plus the local Node-RED runtime this
repo uses to develop and demo it. See the Makefile for the supported
commands (`make help`).

## Running Node-RED

- `make install` - installs node-red/nodemon (root) and this project's
  `data/` userDir dependencies (e.g. the editor theme).
- `make start` / `make dev` - run in the foreground (Ctrl+C to stop).
  Both also write the pid to `data/.node-red.pid`.
- `make stop` - stops a backgrounded `start`/`dev` instance and its child
  processes. This is important because `dev` runs node-red as a child of
  nodemon, and killing nodemon alone leaves node-red running as an orphan
  still bound to the port. The process-tree approach works on both Linux and
  macOS, where `setsid` is not available by default.
- Requires Node 22+ (see `.nvmrc`). Don't `pkill -f "node-red ..."` --
  node-red overwrites its own process title to just `node-red`, so the
  full command line isn't matchable; use `make stop` or kill a pid you
  actually captured (e.g. from `data/.node-red.pid`).
- `make demo` / `make demo-stop` run a *separate* instance against
  `demo/` (own userDir, own port `1881`, own pidfile) seeded from
  `demo/flows.json` -- a showcase flow, not a dev sandbox. It never
  reads or writes `data/flows.json`; use it for a clean, disposable
  round-trip check without disturbing real dev work in `data/`.

## Testing

- If local validation fails or cannot run, use the matching pinned PR CI jobs
  as independent validation. Report local failures and CI results separately;
  do not suppress tests, waive required checks, or claim a local failure passed.
- `make test` (or `npm test` from repo root) -- unit + node-level
  integration tests (`node --test` across `packages/node-red-agents`).
  Offline, no real CLIs invoked, this is the CI-facing gate. Run this
  after any change to `packages/node-red-agents/**`.
- `make test-e2e` -- smoke/E2E suite (`test/integration/`): boots a real,
  throwaway Node-RED instance and shells out to the real `gh`/`opencode`
  CLIs. CI runs independent, exact-version-pinned OpenCode v1 (`opencode-ai`)
  and v2 (`@opencode/cli`) jobs against the same smoke flows, setting each
  adapter's version mode explicitly. Bump these global CLI pins manually
  after verifying the candidate versions and smoke behavior; Dependabot
  cannot track global installs declared only in workflow run commands. The
  v1 job retains the required `E2E` check name; `E2E v2` is an additional
  check not currently required by the main-branch ruleset. Deliberately not
  part of `make test`; local runs require installed and authenticated CLIs.
- `make test-model-e2e` -- opt-in real OpenRouter model/decision/credential and
  OpenCode shared-auth acceptance. Requires `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and incurs provider
  billing; Gateway runs when `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` exists. See `/docs/model-e2e.md`.
  `E2E_OPENCODE_MODEL` optionally selects an authenticated model for the existing
  smoke suite without changing its CI default.
- `NODE_RED_AGENTS_OPENCODE_MODE=v2 make test-model-e2e` selects explicit v2
  adapters/auth selectors; the model suite's omitted mode retains v1.
  `make test-v2-acceptance` runs pinned v2.0.28 cwd, multi-tool/durable-idle,
  pagination, subagent policy and active server recovery plus Direct/SRT CLI
  cancellation. Requires OpenRouter credentials and SRT, incurs billing, and is
  separate from fork-safe CI. See `/docs/model-e2e.md` for isolation and evidence.
- `make format` / `make lint` -- Prettier / ESLint (flat config,
  `eslint.config.js`); pass `FIX=1` to rewrite/auto-fix instead of just
  checking. `make ci` runs format + lint + test + test-e2e, the same
  local gate CI enforces (see
  `.github/workflows/tests.yml`).
- `make audit` -- `npm audit` scoped to what actually matters: the
  published `packages/node-red-agents` package's production deps (fails
  the build only with `STRICT=1`, which `make release` always runs) plus
  an advisory-only pass over the root workspace's dev tooling (Node-RED
  core, ESLint, etc. -- never shipped to consumers, so never build-blocking).
  Deliberately **not** part of `make ci`/`tests.yml`'s per-PR gate: new
  advisories land against unchanged dependency trees, which would make
  the PR gate fail for reasons unrelated to the diff under review.
  Instead, `.github/workflows/audit.yml` runs `make audit STRICT=1` on a
  weekly schedule plus `workflow_dispatch`. `.github/dependabot.yml` keeps
  the root npm workspace (covers `packages/node-red-agents` via npm
  workspaces -- it has no lockfile of its own) and the GitHub Actions used
  in our own workflows up to date; `data/`/`demo/`'s own `package-lock.json`
  files are intentionally excluded since they're gitignored/regenerable
  local dev state, not durable Dependabot targets.
  `.github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml` requests GitHub's native
  auto-merge (not an instant merge -- it still waits on the branch
  ruleset's required status checks: Format + Lint, Unit + Integration, E2E)
  for Dependabot PRs that are patch/minor bumps of dev dependencies or
  GitHub Actions only. Production dependency bumps and any major bump
  (dev or prod) are deliberately excluded and always need a human to
  merge, since those are the changes most likely to carry breaking or
  security-relevant behavior for consumers of the published package.

## Releasing

- `make release BUMP=patch|minor|major` bumps
  `packages/node-red-agents/package.json`'s version, commits, and tags
  `node-red-agents@<version>`. Refuses to run on a dirty tree or if
  `make test` fails.
- **Primary path:** `git push --follow-tags` after `make release` triggers
  `.github/workflows/publish.yml`, which publishes
  `@tbrandenburg/node-red-agents` to npm via
  [OIDC trusted publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers) --
  no `NPM_TOKEN` secret exists or is needed. The workflow re-verifies the
  tag matches `package.json`'s version and that
  `packages/node-red-agents/` at HEAD matches what the tag pointed at (same
  tree-content check as `make publish` below), runs `make test`, then
  `npm publish --access public` and `gh release create ... --generate-notes`
  (skipped if the release already exists). The npmjs.com package has a
  Trusted Publisher registered for `tbrandenburg/node-red-agents` /
  `publish.yml` / `npm publish` -- the workflow filename must keep matching
  that exactly. `workflow_dispatch` (default `dry_run: true`) and any PR
  touching `publish.yml` (harness-only: checkout, test, `npm pack
  --dry-run`, no npm auth or release) exist to validate the workflow
  without publishing for real.
- **Manual/local fallback:** `make publish` verifies the tree is clean,
  `packages/node-red-agents/` at HEAD matches what the version's tag
  pointed at (a tree-content check, not a literal HEAD == tag-commit
  check -- unrelated commits after tagging don't block a release), and
  `make test` passes, then runs the real `npm publish` -- which needs
  the human's own npm OTP (2FA), so an agent should never attempt to
  complete this step itself. On a real (non-dry-run) publish, it also
  creates the matching GitHub Release via `gh release create
  ... --generate-notes` (skips cleanly if `gh` isn't available/authed or
  the release already exists) -- so a plain git tag from `make release`
  is not yet "released" until `make publish` (or the CI workflow) actually
  runs. Use `PUBLISH_DRY_RUN=1 make publish` to rehearse every
  precondition without publishing or creating a release.

## Custom nodes

- `packages/node-red-agents/nodes/<name>/` holds all custom nodes
  (`agent`, `agent-server`, `gh`, and any new ones), published together
  as the single `@tbrandenburg/node-red-agents` npm package
  (`packages/node-red-agents/package.json`'s `node-red.nodes` map lists
  all of them). It's linked into `data/` via npm workspaces
  (`data/package.json`'s `@tbrandenburg/node-red-agents` dependency) --
  restarting Node-RED is enough to pick up a new node, no palette
  install step.
- `make new-node-package NAME=x` scaffolds
  `packages/node-red-agents/nodes/x/` (JS, HTML, starter test) and
  registers it in `packages/node-red-agents/package.json` via
  `scripts/register-node.js`.
- Nodes needing their own npm deps:
  `cd packages/node-red-agents && npm install <pkg>` (shared across all
  nodes in the package -- there is no per-node dependency isolation).
- `POST /nodes {"module": "<absolute path>"}` against the admin API (see
  below) is only needed for installing a *separate*, not-yet-workspaced
  package (e.g. while prototyping outside `packages/node-red-agents`).
- After editing the JS/HTML of an *already-loaded* node, Node-RED must be
  **restarted** to pick up the change (re-POSTing to `/nodes` just replies
  `module_already_loaded`; there's no hot-reload for installed node code).
- `data/nodes/` is for quick single-file drop-in nodes (no packaging) --
  see `data/nodes/README.md`.

## Controlling a running instance from the shell (Admin HTTP API)

No browser needed; the same API the editor UI uses is directly callable:

- `GET /flows` - full current flow JSON (array of tabs/nodes).
- `POST /flows` (JSON array body) - deploy a full flow config, `204` on success.
- `POST /inject/<nodeId>` - fire an inject node.
- `POST /nodes {"module": "<path-or-npm-name>"}` - install/link a node package.

## Editing large flow files without loading the whole thing (nr-mcp)

`demo/flows.json` (and `data/flows.json`) hold every tab in one JSON array
-- 300+ nodes as of the Agentic Development Team tab. Hand-editing that via
`Read`/`Edit`/`Write` means holding the entire file in context for even a
one-field change, and risks touching unrelated nodes. `.opencode/opencode.jsonc`
configures the `nr-mcp` MCP server
(https://github.com/Texan-NXTassist/nr-mcp) for exactly this: it reads/writes
one tab or node at a time via the same Admin API endpoints listed above (`GET`
`/flows` once, `POST /flows` with the `rev` field for optimistic locking --
never `PUT /flow/:id`, which silently reorders tabs), so a single-tab fetch of
even the biggest tab here is ~30% of the full file's bytes and shrinks further
for any smaller tab.

- Points at `http://localhost:1881` (the `make demo` instance) by default --
  change `NR_URL` in `opencode.jsonc` if editing `data/flows.json` against
  `make dev`/`make start` (port 1880) instead.
- Requires `uv`/`uvx` on `PATH`. Uses `uvx --with "mcp==1.9.4" nr-mcp` --
  the plain `uvx nr-mcp` invocation fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No
  module named 'mcp.server.fastmcp'` because the latest `mcp` package
  resolved by `uvx` removed that import path; pinning `mcp==1.9.4` (verified
  working) fixes it without touching nr-mcp's own code.
- No Node-RED auth is configured in `demo/settings.js`/`data/settings.js`,
  so no `NR_USER`/`NR_PASS`/`NR_TOKEN` is needed for local dev.
- The Node-RED instance must actually be running (`make demo` or
  `make dev`/`make start`) for the MCP server's tool calls to succeed --
  it's a thin client over the Admin API, not a standalone flow parser.

## Observing live results (debug/status) without a browser

By default, debug nodes only show output in the editor's browser sidebar
(`console` option off) -- nothing is printed to the node-red process log.
To see it from the shell:

- Connect a WebSocket to `ws://<host>:<port>/comms` (**plural** -- `/comm`
  looks like it hangs: node-red's upgrade handler silently ignores an
  unrecognized path instead of rejecting the connection, so a wrong path
  just times out with zero bytes, which looks like a bug but isn't one).
- After connecting, send `{"subscribe":"debug"}` and/or
  `{"subscribe":"status/#"}` -- nothing arrives until you subscribe.
- Messages arrive as JSON arrays of `{topic, data}`. Debug events have
  `topic:"debug"` and `data.id` = the debug node's id; status events have
  `topic:"status/<nodeId>"`.
- Node 22+ has a built-in global `WebSocket`/`fetch` -- no need to `npm
  install ws` for a throwaway script.

## Round-tripping changes (react, don't sleep-and-poll)

Firing an inject with `curl` and then `sleep N` before checking a log file
wastes time (fixed delay tax on top of the real run time) and is flaky
(N might still be too short). Instead, use a script that subscribes over
`/comms`, triggers the inject itself, and returns the instant the target
debug/status event arrives, with a timeout only as a safety net:

```
node scripts/run-and-watch.js <injectNodeId> <debugNodeId> [maxWaitMs]
```

Typical workflow for iterating on someone's live flow:

1. `GET /flows` to read the current graph and find the relevant node ids.
2. Edit the JSON, `POST /flows` to deploy (`204` = success).
3. `node scripts/run-and-watch.js <injectId> <debugId>` to run it and get
   the result back as soon as it's actually ready.

## Debugging a flow from the shell

Use the runtime APIs instead of Playwright when debugging a flow:

1. Read the current graph: `curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:1880/flows`.
2. Identify the inject node, target node, and a debug node connected to the
   output under test.
3. For a flow without a debug node, deploy a temporary copy that adds one,
   run the test, then restore the original flow from the saved `GET /flows`
   response. Do not overwrite `data/flows.json` with test-only nodes.
4. Run `node scripts/run-and-watch.js <injectId> <debugId> [maxWaitMs]`.
   It subscribes to `/comms`, injects the message, and prints the first
   matching result or red node status.
5. If the watcher times out, subscribe to `status/#` and `debug` directly
   with a small Node 22+ WebSocket script to distinguish node status, output,
   and transport problems. Check the Node-RED process log for node errors.

Always restore temporary deployments, verify `POST /flows` returns `204`,
and check `git diff` before finishing. For nodes that spawn child processes,
use captured PIDs or `make stop`; never use broad `pkill` patterns.

## child_process gotchas (nodes that shell out, e.g. agent, opencode-run)

`spawn()`'s default stdio leaves the child's stdin open as an unclosed
pipe. Some CLIs (e.g. `opencode`) hang indefinitely waiting on it instead
of behaving like a normal non-interactive invocation. Always pass
`stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']` when spawning a child that isn't
meant to read stdin.

## Data hygiene

- `data/flows.json` / `data/flows_cred.json` are real, potentially
  unsaved user work created through the browser editor -- never delete
  or reset them as "test cleanup" without checking first.
- `data/node_modules/`, `data/package-lock.json`, `data/.config.*.json`,
  `data/lib/`, `data/.node-red.pid` are regenerable and gitignored --
  safe to delete freely.
- `demo/flows.json` is also intentionally tracked -- it's the demo flow
  (see `docs/260817_Refactoring.md` step 13), curated by hand, not
  test-only scratch content. `demo/node_modules/`, `demo/package-lock.json`,
  `demo/.config.*.json`, `demo/.node-red.pid` are regenerable and
  gitignored, same as their `data/` counterparts.

## Lessons Learned

- 2026-11-10: Pitfall: An agent edited and tested the coordinator tree instead of its assigned worktree. Prevention rule/countermeasure: Verify `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and branch before every edit or validation run.
- 2026-11-10: Pitfall: Process diagnostics exposed an API key in command arguments. Prevention rule/countermeasure: Inspect process IDs, names, and resource usage without printing full command lines.
- 2026-11-10: Pitfall: A catalog's chat-filtered response included embedding and extraction models. Prevention rule/countermeasure: Verify upstream classification against model metadata and disclose uncertainty when its type labels are unreliable.
- 2026-11-09: Pitfall: Local OpenCode E2E workarounds created nonrepresentative profiles and produced inconsistent results. Prevention rule/countermeasure: Prefer the pinned, clean CI v1/v2 jobs before constructing alternate local environments; report local failures separately.
- 2026-11-09: Pitfall: npm 10 stripped existing platform `libc` metadata during validation installs. Prevention rule/countermeasure: Inspect the final lockfile diff after running install-backed checks and preserve unrelated platform metadata.
- 2026-10-15: Pitfall: Cancellation entered retry-all, and escalation trusted an exited leader's numeric PGID. Prevention: Mark manual cancellation non-retryable; verify surviving owned process identities before post-exit signalling, and test recycled PID/PGID cases.
- 2026-10-15: Pitfall: A model transcribed a random absolute cancellation-script path incorrectly. Prevention: Use a short cwd-relative command, retain a unique bounded process title for host-PID capture, and fail unless the actual tool and descendant are active.
- 2026-10-14: Pitfall: Native v2 shell was searched through Code Mode and returned no matches. Prevention: Native shell has `codemode: false`; invoke its top-level tool directly and require an active PID/file before accepting cancellation.
- 2026-10-14: Pitfall: Awaiting a nested test scheduled on the outer TestContext deadlocked acceptance; custom correlation fields also filtered out lifecycle events. Prevention: Use the current subtest context and correlate lifecycle events by `_msgid`.
- 2026-10-14: Pitfall: An allowlisted SRT environment omitted `CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR`, causing EROFS before CLI launch. Prevention: Include its private writable temp path and use the real CLI-auth sanitizer, not an identity callback.
- 2026-10-13: Pitfall: Recursive credential-key filtering removed legitimate structured fields and decision labels. Prevention rule/countermeasure: Preserve application-defined keys; filter transport metadata separately and test data preservation alongside secret redaction.
- 2026-10-13: Pitfall: Test-helper nodes without a tab were classified as config nodes and self-referenced their type. Prevention rule/countermeasure: Use explicit tab/z fixtures, distinct IDs and bounded readiness waits before running suites.
- 2026-10-13: Pitfall: Failed environment-object assertions printed ambient credentials. Prevention rule/countermeasure: Use synthetic environments and boolean equality checks; never include ambient environment objects in assertion diagnostics.
- 2026-10-03: Pitfall: Runtime-deploy notification preceded Inject endpoint registration under concurrent E2E load. Prevention rule/countermeasure: Check actual Inject endpoint readiness with a bounded retry before triggering assertions; a deployment notification alone is insufficient.
- 2026-09-29: Pitfall: A real Node-RED E2E test assumed deployment made inject endpoints immediately available and Catch messages appeared on a debug node. Prevention rule/countermeasure: Wait for a deployment signal before injecting; inspect actual `/comms` diagnostic events when testing node errors.
- 2026-09-28: Pitfall: A full filesystem blocked git worktrees and truncated a patch write. Prevention rule/countermeasure: Check free disk space on git lock or write failures; reclaim space, restore the affected file, and verify syntax before retrying.
- 2026-09-05: Pitfall: a subagent task can report "user rejected permission" and appear failed even though it already `git commit`ed real, complete work first. Prevention rule/countermeasure: before retrying/redoing, always check the worktree's `git log`/`git status` for prior commits; instruct subagents to commit before their final message.
- 2026-09-26: Pitfall: duplicated a repository prefix in a nested worktree path, triggering avoidable permission errors. Prevention: copy the canonical path from `git worktree list` and use it verbatim in subsequent tool calls.

Optional `text` must be a string. Invalid/malformed responses, undeclared decisions, unknown/expired IDs, duplicate resolutions and unchanged pending Request loopbacks fail through Catch. Do not wire Request directly back unchanged. Branching is ordinary Node-RED wiring, with no built-in approve/reject policy. The `interaction` field is reserved for this protocol: remove a previous result before starting a subsequent Interaction boundary. In stock Node-RED the original message is kept in a process-local map. The input invocation completes after Request emission; no unresolved Promise or active worker waits for the human. **Restart/redeploy loses pending interactions.** A suspension-capable host may persist the wait and resume the same logical interaction in a fresh worker. ### Durable host ABI (version 1) Every live `interaction` node exposes `node.interaction`: - `version: 1`. - `await plan(msg)`: resolve typed Prompt and validate Decisions; return `{version: 1, interactionId: "", nodeId, nodeName, prompt, decisions}`. This emits nothing and inserts nothing into the local map. Requires an ordinary input without `interaction`. The returned metadata is JSON-serializable; IDs are generated once per plan call, so persist and reuse the accepted plan. - `resume(plan, originalMsg, {decision, text?})`: validate version, matching node ID, plan fields and response against the **plan's** decisions, clone the host-restored original using Node-RED's `cloneMessage`, set `interaction`, call real `node.send(msg)` on Continue (output 1), and return the sent message. Acknowledgement has a 60-second transport bound; rejection/timeout fails the input through Catch with no local fallback or retry. A timed-out callback may still commit; the host must reconcile/deduplicate using `plan.interactionId`. The record's `msg` is a Node-RED clone, not a serialized checkpoint: persistence/serialization failures must reject the pause explicitly. # Drop-in custom nodes

`settings.js` sets `nodesDir: 'nodes'`, so Node-RED scans this folder
(and only this folder) for standalone custom nodes: a `<name>.js` file
paired with an optional `<name>.html` file. No `package.json` or
`npm install` required — just add the files and restart Node-RED
(`make dev` restarts automatically on change).

This is the fastest way to prototype a node. `example-lower-case.js/.html`
is a working example — copy the pair, rename, edit.

Once a node is ready to share/publish or needs its own npm dependencies,
scaffold it into the real package via `make new-node-package NAME=my-node`
(from repo root) -- this creates
`../../packages/node-red-agents/nodes/my-node/` (JS, HTML, starter test)
and registers it automatically; no separate palette install step needed,
since `node-red-agents` is already linked into `data/` via npm workspaces.
See `agent` or `gh` under `../../packages/node-red-agents/nodes/` for
real examples.

# node-red-agents

Node-RED nodes for coding agents, direct model requests, typed probabilistic
decisions, human interaction and GitHub CLI operations.

## Nodes

- **agent** — runs a coding-agent CLI (OpenCode first, `pi` also
  supported) either directly or sandboxed via SRT (Anthropic's
  sandbox-runtime), one execution per input message. Also supports
  session resume, `$INPUTS.<name>` templating, retry with session
  reuse, a FIFO concurrency scheduler, on-demand termination, tool
  allow/deny lists, MCP server configuration, structured (JSON-Schema)
  output validation, and cost/token usage reporting where supported.
- **agent-server** — manages a long-lived `opencode serve` daemon
  (session-based), for flows that need repeated low-latency calls
  instead of `agent`'s one-shot execution model. Supports
  `message`/`status`/`abort`/`history`/`terminate` operations, an
  instance cap (`maxInstances`), and optional basic auth. SRT
  sandboxing is **not functional** for this node (see its built-in
  help) since it only sandboxes outbound egress, not the inbound calls
  this node needs.
- **gh** — runs GitHub CLI (`gh`) commands and returns parsed output,
  with structured error classification and per-message overrides.
- **interaction** — human-on-the-loop / human-in-the-loop boundary with one
  input and Continue/Request outputs. Name, typed Prompt and ordered Decisions
  are its editor settings. Ordinary input emits a pending Request; a separate
  later message carrying `interaction.id` and a declared `interaction.decision`
  resumes the stored original message with `{id, decision, text?}` without
  changing payload. Decision meanings belong to ordinary Switch/Change wiring.
  Pending messages are process-local and lost on restart/redeploy; the initial
  invocation completes without waiting for the human. A durable host can use
  the version-1 `node.interaction.plan(msg)` and
  `node.interaction.resume(plan, originalMsg, response)` APIs; the host owns
  checkpointing and deduplication, and resume uses normal Node-RED routing.
  See the [interaction contract and host ABI](https://github.com/tbrandenburg/node-red-agents#human-interaction).
- **model-provider** — reusable OpenRouter or Vercel AI Gateway configuration.
  Stores API keys as native password credentials, separate from flow exports.
  Supports default/allowed models, timeout and trusted-admin custom URLs.
- **model** — direct generation, schema-validated structured output and embeddings
  through the AI SDK, without invoking a coding-agent CLI. Output 1 supplies
  `msg.modelResult`; optional output 2 emits `msg.modelEvent` text deltas.
- **decision** — Jev Boolean, Choice and Score questions with typed probabilities
  and available metadata in `msg.decisionResult`. Use Switch/interaction nodes
  for explicit thresholds and human review.

The agent nodes retain default CLI authentication. Optional shared-provider mode
uses explicit supported provider mappings in child-process environments; saved
CLI authentication may take precedence. Restart server daemons after rotating keys.
See the [provider compatibility and message contracts](https://github.com/tbrandenburg/node-red-agents#direct-models-and-shared-credentials).

See each node's built-in help (Node-RED editor info panel) for
configuration details, or `nodes/gh/README.md` for `gh`-specific usage
and example flows (`nodes/gh/examples/`).

## Requirements

- Node-RED >= 4.0.0, Node.js >= 22 (required by the pinned AI SDK).
- The [`opencode`](https://opencode.ai) CLI on `PATH` (for `agent`/`agent-server`)
- [`srt`](https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime) on `PATH`, only if using the SRT runtime option
- The [`gh`](https://cli.github.com) CLI on `PATH`, authenticated (for `gh`)
- An OpenRouter or AI Gateway API key and supported model IDs for direct model
  and decision requests. Direct SDK nodes do not require a coding-agent CLI.

## Install

```sh
npm install @tbrandenburg/node-red-agents
```

Then restart Node-RED, or install via the editor: **Menu -> Manage
palette -> Install tab -> search "node-red-agents"**.

# node-red-contrib-gh

Runs the installed [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/) (`gh`) from a
Node-RED flow. One `gh` invocation per incoming message, no shell involved.

## Prerequisites

`gh` must already be installed and authenticated on the Node-RED host:

```bash
gh --version
gh auth login          # or GH_TOKEN / GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN in the environment
```

This package does not bundle `gh` or implement its own login flow.

## Node: `gh`

**Inputs:** 1   **Outputs:** 1

| Field              | Type                | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------ | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Command            | str/msg/flow/global | The `gh` subcommand, e.g. `pr`, `issue`, `workflow`, `api`. Not the full command line -- `gh` itself is always the executable and can never be overridden.                                       |
| Arguments          | str/msg/flow/global | Everything after the command, e.g. `list --state open --json number,title,url`. A string value is tokenized (quote-aware, no shell evaluation); an array value (e.g. from `msg.`) is used as-is. |
| Repository         | str/msg/flow/global | Optional `owner/repo`. Sets `GH_REPO` for the invocation.                                                                                                                                        |
| Host (Advanced)    | str                 | Optional GitHub Enterprise hostname, e.g. `github.example.com`. Sets `GH_HOST`.                                                                                                                  |
| Timeout (Advanced) | number (ms)         | Default 60000. The child process is killed (`SIGTERM`) if it runs longer than this.                                                                                                              |

### `msg.gh` overrides

```js
msg.gh = {
  command: "issue",
  args: ["list", "--state", "open"], // array preferred; skips parsing entirely
  repo: "owner/repo",
  host: "github.example.com",
};
```

Any property present on `msg.gh` takes precedence over the node's own
configuration for that message.

### Output

- `msg.payload`: parsed JSON if stdout was valid JSON, otherwise the raw
  stdout string.
- `msg.gh`: `{ command, args, repo, host, exitCode, stderr }` execution
  metadata. Never contains credentials.

A non-zero exit code, a timeout, or a missing `gh` executable all go through
`done(error)` (catchable with a Catch node) instead of producing an output
message. Every such error carries an `err.errorType` string so flows can
branch on it without regex-matching gh's (locale/version dependent) human
-readable stderr text themselves:

| `errorType`        | When                                                                          |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `auth`              | Not logged in / bad credentials (stderr mentions `gh auth login`, etc.)       |
| `rate-limit`        | GitHub API (primary or secondary) rate limit exceeded                        |
| `feature-disabled`  | Repo has issues/PRs/projects disabled (e.g. this ticket's original report)    |
| `not-found`         | Repository/resource doesn't exist or can't be resolved                       |
| `permission`        | 403 / insufficient permissions                                               |
| `network`           | Network failure or timeout talking to GitHub                                 |
| `not-installed`     | `gh` executable not found on `PATH` (spawn `ENOENT`)                          |
| `spawn-failed`      | The child process could not be started for another reason                    |
| `timeout`           | The command exceeded the configured Timeout and was killed                   |
| `killed`            | The command was killed by a signal other than the node's own timeout         |
| `unknown`           | Non-zero exit whose stderr didn't match any known pattern                    |

## Security

- The executable is always the literal string `gh`; nothing in `msg` or

- Credentials are never logged, included in `msg`, or included in errors.

# Refactoring Plan: Node-RED Agents → Publishable Node Library

Date: 2026-08-17
Status: proposed → in progress

## Goal

Turn `custom-nodes/{agent,agent-server,gh}` from four hand-installed
islands into a single, publishable, FlowFuse-Dashboard-style npm package
(`node-red-agents`, workspace-managed), while:

- keeping `data/` as the untouched local dev userDir (real, unsaved work),
- extracting a separate `demo/` userDir seeded from today's
  `data/flows.json`,
- adding a real test pyramid (unit / node-level integration / smoke E2E)
  that runs offline and gates regressions on every node change,
- never reducing the currently-passing test count at any step.

## Why (see full analysis in session, summarized)

- Current state: each node package (`agent`, `agent-server`) is
  internally well-factored (`lib/` + mirrored `test/`), but there is no
  workspace tying them together, no root test runner, no shared code
  path (duplication has already started: `srt-settings.js` is a verbatim
  copy between `agent` and `agent-server`, admitted in its own comment),
  and every `package.json` is missing publish-required fields
  (license, repository, files, engines, node-red.version).
- FlowFuse's `@flowfuse/node-red-dashboard` ships 27 nodes as **one**
  npm package with shared internals — not a multi-package monorepo. We
  have exactly that shared-internals situation and none of the pressure
  (different release cadence, users wanting one node without another)
  that would justify separate publishable packages.
- `data/flows.json` is documented in this repo's own `.gitignore` /
  AGENTS.md as real, potentially-unsaved user work — it must not also be
  the demo flow or the smoke-test fixture. Three different flows, three
  different pressures (dev sandbox vs. pretty demo vs. ugly-but-precise
  regression check).

# Agentic Development Team — demo flow plan

Status: **plan / for review** (nothing implemented yet)
Date: 2026-08-20
Target: new tab + dashboard page in `demo/flows.json` (demo instance, port 1881)

---

## 1. Goal

A fourth showcase tab, **Agentic Development Team**, that continuously watches a
GitHub repository and keeps up to 3 agents per category busy on its open issues,
open pull requests and recent Actions runs — with a start/stop schedule, live
per-item state tables, and a chronological agent-event trace.

Everything runs **read-only against the remote**: agents work exclusively in
local, per-task git worktrees, and their output is deliberately thrown away.
This is a demonstration of orchestration, not a production automation.

## 2. Constraints discovered in the existing code

These drive most of the design decisions below.

1. **`scripts/ensure-repo.sh` is not safe for concurrent agents.** It maintains
   *one* clone per repo (`workspace/<owner>__<repo>`) and runs
   `fetch && checkout && reset --hard && clean -fd` on every invocation. The
   `arw-repo-gate` lock inside `arw-subflow` serialises only the clone step, not
   the agent run. Nine concurrent agents sharing that directory would corrupt
   each other's work. → per-task worktrees are mandatory (§4).
2. **The existing prompts assume the agent creates its own worktree.**
   `prompts/fix-issue.md` instructs `git worktree add …`, and
   `prompts/investigate-issue.md` ends with `gh issue comment` — a remote write.
   → a new, separate prompt set is required (§5).
3. **`arw-subflow` cannot be interrupted.** It has no terminate path to its
   internal `agent` node, and its outputs don't expose an `executionId` at
   dispatch time. Retrofitting both would risk regressing the Issue Control
   Center. → a new, ADT-specific subflow instead (§6).
4. **The `agent` node (0.2.0) already provides what we need:** a per-run
   `executionId` on output 2's event envelope (`msg.executionId`) and on
   output 1 (`msg.agentExecution.id`), plus a terminate input
   (`msg.operation = "terminate"` + `msg.executionId`, addressed to the *same*
   node instance). `msg.agentId` is the node id — constant across concurrent
   runs of one node — so the tables key on `executionId`.

## 4. Workspace isolation (outcome, not mechanism)

**Required outcome:** every agent run starts in its own, already-prepared git
worktree of the target repo, checked out on the default branch, isolated from
every other concurrent run; the agent never has to create or reason about
worktrees itself.

**Chosen mechanism:** a new `scripts/ensure-worktree.sh <host> <owner> <repo>
<taskKey>`, kept deliberately small:

- maintains one shared **base clone** at `workspace/<owner>__<repo>.base`
  (`clone` if absent, then `fetch origin`) — the only step needing the existing
  per-repo lock;
- derives the default branch the same way `ensure-repo.sh` does;
- creates (or reuses) a worktree at
  `workspace/<owner>__<repo>--<taskKey>` on a task branch
  `adt/<taskKey>` based on `origin/<defaultBranch>`;
- **idempotent**: if the worktree directory already exists and is a valid
  worktree, it is reset to `origin/<defaultBranch>` and cleaned rather than
  recreated — so a task that was hard-stopped and later retried under the same
  `taskKey` just works;
- prints `REPO_DIR=` / `DEFAULT_BRANCH=` exactly like `ensure-repo.sh`, so the
  downstream parsing logic is unchanged.

`taskKey` is deterministic per task and phase:
`issue-<n>`, `issue-<n>-fix`, `pr-<n>`, `run-<id>`.

**Lifecycle:** worktrees are *not* removed when a task ends. They are pruned at
the beginning of every **Start**: `scripts/prune-worktrees.sh <owner> <repo>`
removes every `workspace/<owner>__<repo>--*` directory and runs
`git worktree prune` in the base clone. This keeps results inspectable between
runs and bounds disk growth to one schedule cycle.

**Update (huge-repo demo hardening):** the base-clone-or-fetch step (the only
one needing the per-repo lock) was extracted into its own
`scripts/prime-base.sh <host> <owner> <repo>`, callable standalone via a
dashboard "Prime Base" button (between Update and Start) so a large repo's
initial clone can be triggered ahead of time instead of blocking whichever
task happens to run first. `ensure-worktree.sh` now calls `prime-base.sh`
rather than duplicating that logic. The base clone itself was also switched
to `git clone --bare` — it is only ever used as a `git worktree add` source,
never checked out directly, so a bare clone is both the conventional git
pattern for this and saves one full working tree of disk. Note bare clones do
not set up a `refs/remotes/origin/*` refspec the way a normal clone does
(they copy `refs/heads/*` directly); `prime-base.sh` configures
`remote.origin.fetch` explicitly so `origin/<defaultBranch>` still resolves
for worktree creation. Progress/success/failure is surfaced via a
`ui-notification` toast; there is no button-disable/enable state to manage.

`ensure-repo.sh` and the Issue Control Center are left untouched.

## 5. Prompts — `prompts/read-only/`

Four new files. All of them:

- state that the agent is **already inside an isolated worktree** at the current
  directory, and must **not** create worktrees, switch branches, commit, push,
  or open/comment on anything;
- restrict `gh` usage to read-only subcommands (`view`, `diff`, `list`,
  `run view --log`);
- ask for the result to be **printed to stdout** (it is captured as the agent's
  payload and shown in the trace), never written to the remote;
- keep the analysis intentionally shallow/cheap — this is a showcase.

| File | Used by | Placeholders |
|---|---|---|
| `investigate-issue.md` | Issues, phase 1 | `{{repoSlug}}`, `{{defaultBranch}}`, `{{issueNumber}}` |
| `fix-issue.md` | Issues, phase 2 | same |
| `review-pr.md` | Pull Requests | `{{prNumber}}` |
| `investigate-action.md` | Actions | `{{runId}}`, `{{workflowName}}`, `{{conclusion}}` |

Note on `fix-issue.md`: because each subflow run gets a fresh worktree, the fix
phase cannot inherit the investigation's context. The prompt therefore
re-establishes context itself (`gh issue view`) and then edits files **locally
only**, summarising the resulting diff (`git diff`) on stdout. Nothing is
committed. The table state is labelled simply **Fixed** — no PR is created.

Loaded via `file in` nodes with paths relative to the repo root
(`prompts/read-only/…`), matching the existing Issue Control Center convention.

## 6. New subflow: `adt-task-subflow`

Rather than extending `arw-subflow` (regression risk for the Issue Control
Center, and it lacks a terminate path), ADT gets its own small subflow —
one definition, **four instances**: Issue Investigate, Issue Fix, PR Review,
Action Investigate.

**Input msg:** `{ context, promptTemplate }` where
`context = {host, owner, repo, model, kind, itemId, taskKey, phase}`.

**Internal path:**

```
in ─▶ [switch: operation]
        ├ terminate ──────────────────────────────────▶ (agent node, terminate input)
        └ normal ─▶ [build args] ─▶ [exec ensure-worktree.sh]
                    ─▶ [handle result: parse REPO_DIR/DEFAULT_BRANCH]
                    ─▶ [GATE: schedule still running?]     ← the only abort point
                    ─▶ [render prompt template]
                    ─▶ [agent] ─▶ [handle result]
```

**Outputs:**

1. **completion** — `{context, status, payload}` (success or failure); drives the
   phase transition and frees the concurrency slot.
2. **agent events** — the `agent` node's output 2, verbatim; drives the Agent
   column (first `running` event carries the `executionId`) and the trace table.
3. **log/error rows** — worktree failures, gate aborts, prompt-render problems.

**The gate** is the whole of the stop-during-setup story, and is deliberately the
simplest thing that satisfies the priority *"the agent must not be started"*: a
one-line function node immediately before the `agent` node that drops the message
if `global.adt_running` is false. Nothing else in the pipeline is interruptible —
a `git fetch` may finish after Stop was pressed, which costs a second and zero
tokens. No generation counters, no cancellation plumbing.

## 7. State model

All in **global** context (not `flow`): the `adt-task-subflow` instances have
their own private flow context, separate from the tab's, so anything the gate
or dispatch logic needs to see from both places must be global. (Discovered
during M3 verification — the plan originally said `flow.adt_*`.)

```js
global.adt_ctx     = { host, owner, repo, model }
global.adt_running = false                       // schedule on/off
global.adt_max     = { issue: 3, pr: 3, action: 3 }
global.adt_tasks   = {
  issue:  { "42": { id, title, phase, executionId, updatedAt }, … },
  pr:     { "17": { … } },
  action: { "99123": { …, workflowName, conclusion } },
}
```

Phases and their table glyphs:

| kind | phases |
|---|---|
| issue | ⬜ not_started → ⏳ in_progress *(investigate)* → ⏳ in_progress *(fix)* → 🔧 fixed; 🔒 closed |
| pr | ⬜ not_started → ⏳ in_progress → 👀 reviewed; 🔒 closed/merged |
| action | ⬜ not_started → ⏳ in_progress → 🔍 investigated |

Investigation of issues surfaces as 🔍 only transiently — the chain moves
straight on to the fix phase, occupying the *same* concurrency slot throughout
(one slot per issue for both phases, as agreed).

Table columns per group: `State | # | Title | Agent`, where **Agent** shows the
run's `executionId` (short form) while in progress, and is cleared on completion.

## 8. Control flow

### Refresh (Update button, and every tick while running)

Three `gh` calls in parallel:

| kind | command |
|---|---|
| issue | `gh issue list --state open --limit 20 --json number,title,state` |
| pr | `gh pr list --state open --limit 20 --json number,title,state` |
| action | `gh run list --limit 20 --json databaseId,name,status,conclusion` |

Each feeds a **reconcile** function node that merges the fresh list into
`global.adt_tasks[kind]`, **preserving existing phases and executionIds**:

- id not yet tracked → `not_started`;
- tracked id no longer in the open list → `closed` (issues/PRs only);
- everything else keeps its phase.

Actions are investigated **regardless of conclusion** — green runs for
continuous-improvement suggestions, red runs for failure analysis — and have no
`closed` phase.

Reconcile then re-renders that group's table and hands off to dispatch.

### Schedule

A single `inject` with `repeat: 30`, whose first node returns `null` unless
`global.adt_running` is true.

- **Start** → prune worktrees, set `global.adt_running = true`, fire one immediate
  tick.
- **Stop** → set `global.adt_running = false`, then sweep: for every task with an
  `executionId`, emit `{operation:"terminate", executionId, kind}` routed by a
  `switch` on `kind` into the matching subflow instance. Terminated tasks are
  reset to ⬜ *not_started* and their Agent cell cleared, so the next Start
  retries them against the same (idempotent) `taskKey`. The sweep is scoped to
  ADT-tracked executionIds only — Issue Control Center and Chat agents are
  untouched.

### Dispatch

Per group, after each reconcile: count `in_progress`; while
`count < global.adt_max[kind]`, take the next `not_started` item, mark it
`in_progress`, and send it into that group's subflow instance with the
corresponding prompt template. Issue completions of the *investigate* phase
re-enter dispatch as an immediate *fix* dispatch for the same issue (slot never
released in between). Errors from output 3 clear the slot too, so a failure
cannot permanently wedge the concurrency counter.

### Traces

Subflow output 2 from all four instances → one flatten function (reusing the
Issue Control Center's `icc-flatten-agent-log` shape) → prepend to a
`global.adt_trace` array capped at **50** rows, newest first → `ui-table`.

- **default** (including omitted fields in existing flows): preserve the CLI's
  existing login/config and inherited environment. Ignore `modelProvider` and do
  not change model selection. This also preserves Copilot OAuth behavior.
- **provider**: resolve `getProviderConfig` inside each launch, override only the
  mapped API-key variable in a fresh child environment, and select the shared
  default model when the node's Model is blank. A Model override must use the
  matching **CLI** prefix and its remaining upstream ID must equal `defaultModel`
  or appear in `allowedModels`. For example, shared `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4`
  becomes `openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4`. A mismatched CLI provider fails
  before launch rather than silently using another account/provider.
- **environment**: ignore `modelProvider` completely (a config node/key is not
  required). Require an explicit supported CLI `provider/model` and a nonblank
  mapped key in the Node-RED process environment. Copy the inherited environment;
  do not inject a shared key, remap variables, change the selected model, remove
  saved authentication, or force environment precedence. This is a validated
  ambient-key mode, **not** an environment-only authentication isolation mode.

Messages cannot override these modes or select another credential config node.
Missing credentials, unsupported combinations and model mismatches report errors.
Shared custom base URLs are rejected: the SDK URL is not automatically a compatible
CLI endpoint. This feature does not write CLI configuration or authentication files,
nor change `process.env`. Existing CLI configuration still controls CLI endpoints,
extensions, auxiliary models, and authentication behavior.

## Authentication precedence and research

Environment injection offers a key to the CLI; it does **not** guarantee the billed
account. Saved API keys, OAuth, configured API keys, plugins, model settings or an
existing OpenCode v2 managed server can take precedence. Use an independently
provisioned, isolated CLI profile for account-sensitive deployments. This feature
never reads or changes the user's saved credentials to enforce precedence.

## Rotation and redaction

Agent credentials resolve after a queued execution acquires a slot and its start
observer acknowledges, immediately before adapter validation/build and runtime
execution. Every retry/reask resolves again. Credentials/environment are kept out
of the resolved input and observer input record. Existing children keep their
launch environment until exit.

Agent-server resolves a fresh credential immediately before daemon spawn, after
port allocation/version detection. Running daemons keep their original key. After
rotating the shared credential, send `msg.operation="terminate"` with each tracked
`sessionID`, then start messages **without** that ID, or redeploy agent-server to
close its tracked children. Provider-config redeploy alone does not update a running
daemon's environment. Reused sessions still validate the requested provider/model.

Agent-server checks assistant errors even when the daemon returns HTTP 200: v1
uses `info.error` (`name`/`data`), while v2 uses `assistant.error`
(`type`/`message`/`status`). These failures emit a `failed` lifecycle event, clear
the session's busy state, and reach Catch without a final reply or `completed`
event, including when partial text exists. Catch messages use fixed error labels
and authentication/request-failure descriptions; raw provider messages, response
bodies, headers and causes are not forwarded. The daemon remains tracked for
reuse or explicit termination.

Response contracts: [v1 SDK types](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.2.27/packages/sdk/js/src/gen/types.gen.ts),
[v2.0.18 assistant schema](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.0.18/packages/schema/src/session-message.ts)
and [v2.0.18 error schema](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.0.18/packages/schema/src/session-error.ts).

Known injected and inherited API-key/token/password/secret values and their URL,
JSON-escaped and Base64 representations are redacted from parsed child events,
stderr-derived errors, results, terminal observer records and daemon replies/history.
Application field names (including `token`, `secret`, `headers` and `password`)
are preserved; known credential values and Bearer tokens are redacted. CLI event
and stderr diagnostics additionally remove transport/auth header fields and redact
Basic-auth tokens, including those inside JSON diagnostic text. Application
payload/output fields retain their names and values except known credentials. Cyclic
application messages are cloned with their references intact; external diagnostics
are depth-bounded. Sanitizers retain old launch keys for daemon responses after
rotation. OpenCode text/reasoning events buffer possible known-credential prefixes
across parsed events before live emission, observer notification or final retention.
Safe text may be emitted in smaller events with the original structured metadata.
This protects the package's emitted data; CLI-owned files, external plugin logs and
arbitrary transformations outside the listed encodings are outside this guarantee.

# Decision node

`decision` uses a shared `model-provider` config and the pinned AI SDK's
`experimental_decide`. It preserves the original message and adds
`msg.decisionResult`. It has one input and one output; routing and human review
are flow policy.

## Inputs

Select a provider, optionally choose an allowed model ID, and enter State JSON
and Questions JSON. Blank model uses the provider's default. State is a JSON
string, object or data array. Arrays are wrapped in an SDK JSON state part;
this MVP does not accept multimodal/file parts or download state URLs.
Message overrides are parsed values:

```js
msg.decision = {
  state: { message: "I was charged twice. Please refund the duplicate." },
  questions: {
    refund: {
      type: "boolean",
      instructions: "Is the customer requesting a refund?",
      criteria: { true: "Refund requested", false: "No refund requested" },
    },
    department: {
      type: "choice",
      instructions: "Which team should handle this?",
      criteria: { billing: "Charges and refunds", support: "Technical help", other: null },
    },
    severity: {
      type: "score",
      instructions: "How severe is the issue?",
      criteria: ["Cosmetic", "Workaround exists", "Blocking; no workaround"],
    },
  },
};
```

Only `state`, `questions`, and `model` are accepted in `msg.decision`. Unknown
fields (including credentials, URLs, headers and provider options) fail before
provider creation. Questions must be a nonempty map with nonblank names and
`boolean`, `choice`, or `score` types. Instructions and descriptions accept
JSON-compatible strings, objects and arrays. Boolean criteria are optional,
but if supplied must contain both nonnull `true` and `false` descriptions.
Choice criteria require nonblank labels; null descriptions are allowed for a
catch-all option. Score criteria require at least two nonnull ordered levels,
indexed from zero. Extra question options are rejected. Cycles, class instances,
undefined values and nonfinite numbers fail validation before a model call.

## Output and errors

`decisionResult.answers` retains named typed answers:

- Boolean: `{ type: "boolean", probability: 0.8 }`, meaning P(true).
- Choice: `{ type: "choice", choice: "billing", probabilities?: { ... } }`.
- Score: `{ type: "score", score: 1.25, probabilities?: { "0": ..., "1": ... } }`.

The actual SDK validates missing answers, types, ranges, selected labels,
distribution sums and weighted scores. Invalid results produce an error, with
no success output. Rounding tolerances come from SDK `rounding`; returned values
are unchanged even if rounded probabilities sum to 0.99. No normalization or
conversion to binary truth occurs.

Available `rounding`, `usage`, `warnings`, `providerMetadata` and sanitized
`response` are retained by the shared adapter. Optional distributions, confidence,
cost and token counts are not invented. Provider-specific confidence/cost may
appear in metadata and are not a portable probability measure. Secret-bearing
metadata, request bodies and headers are removed/redacted by the shared adapter.
Attach a Catch node for fixed safe errors: local invalid input uses
`INVALID_DECISION_INPUT`; provider/auth/timeout/cancellation codes follow the
[shared provider contract](/docs/model-provider.md). Retries are disabled.
Closing/redeploying the node aborts its own controller for each active input.

## Scenarios and billing boundaries

- Generate a short response, preserve the input, emit exactly one final result.
- Reject non-text input, malformed JSON schema, and empty decision questions
  through native Catch before **zero observed provider fetches**. Each malformed
  case uses a fresh runtime and a synthetic invalid credential.
- Produce a schema-bound structured object with `answer: "pong"`.
- Stream text deltas and one final result; joined deltas must equal final text.
  Observation includes a 350 ms terminal quiet window to catch duplicate results.
- Produce a finite numeric embedding vector from a real embedding request.
- Ask Jev Boolean/Choice/Score together in one short request, validate typed
  answers and bounded probabilities/scores using the runtime's actual SDK.
- Inspect native `/flows` export and `flows.json` for credential exclusion;
  inspect the encrypted `$` envelope in `flows_cred.json`; stop and restart with
  the same userDir/credential secret and successfully generate again.
- Import that export into a second userDir without credentials and require
  `MISSING_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL`, no success, and zero provider fetches.
- Rotate through native credential deployment to a synthetic invalid key,
  require real HTTP 401/403 and `PROVIDER_AUTH` through Catch without leaks,
  restore the live key, and successfully generate again.
- Optional Gateway generation and three-question Jev acceptance run only when
  `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` exists, using `typesafe-ai/jev`. Missing Gateway credentials
  produce an explicit skip reason, never a passing provider result. These are
  two Gateway probes, not a complete duplication of the OpenRouter lifecycle suite.
- Run `agent` with omitted new auth fields and an explicitly selected
  `openrouter/openai/gpt-4.1-nano` model using inherited CLI authentication, then
  independently run shared-provider authentication with blank model selection.
  Separate isolated profiles prevent ambient credentials from proving shared auth.
- Run `agent-server` with shared credentials, terminate its session, redeploy with
  an invalid credential and require Catch with no final success, then restore the
  real credential and verify a new daemon/session returns a response.

Each SDK operation makes one short request; SDK retries are disabled by the
implementation. A successful OpenRouter pass makes eight SDK requests including
the intentionally invalid-key request. Three Jev types share one request. Initial
auth/generation failure stops subsequent scenarios. Provider requests have a
55000 ms deadline, observation has a 65000 ms deadline, admin requests have a
10000 ms deadline, and startup has a 30000 ms deadline. OpenCode receives one
short prompt per mode, denied tool permissions, and a 55000 ms execution deadline;
CLI-internal auxiliary requests remain controlled by the installed CLI.

## Credential, profile and process isolation

The parent consumes keys programmatically. It submits them only in native
Node-RED password credential provisioning via loopback Admin HTTP, not in flow
exports, assertion objects, command arguments, or CLI configuration. The
Node-RED child starts without inherited API keys/tokens/secrets except in the
explicit default-CLI-auth scenario, which inherits only the OpenRouter key.
Shared CLI auth must resolve the native credential rather than use an ambient key.
Observable debug traffic, flow/credential storage and runtime logs are checked
for plaintext, URL-encoded and Base64 credentials; failure reports carry only
safe errors and provider route/status diagnostics, never headers or raw bodies.

The focused launcher uses the package's actual `node-red.nodes` registration
via `nodesDir`. It uses the worktree's own `npm ci` installation without creating
dependency symlinks. It does not touch `data/`, `demo/`, or existing services.
`ss -H -ltn` runs before each runtime/CLI launch; Node-RED binds `127.0.0.1:0`
directly. OpenCode receives loopback hostname configuration (its config schema
rejects port zero). Teardown sends signals only to the captured Node-RED child,
waits for its exit, and removes the temporary directory. Node close owns its CLI
child cleanup. No process-name or command-pattern killing is used.

CLI HOME and XDG config/data/cache/state directories are disposable. Its cwd is
outside the repository, inherited `OPENCODE_*` settings are removed, and inline
config disables updates/sharing and denies tools. No user's saved auth store is
read or modified. In production, shared-provider environment injection does not
override saved account/config precedence; see [CLI provider auth](/docs/cli-provider-auth.md).

`NODE_RED_AGENTS_OPENCODE_MODE=v1|v2` selects both the explicit agent auth selector

# Model provider foundation

Issues #67 and #68 supply a reusable `model-provider` config node and a
CommonJS-to-ESM adapter for trusted execution nodes. No HTTP endpoint exposes
credentials. This foundation does not add model or decision execution nodes.

## Configuration and credentials

The config node stores `name`, `provider` (`openrouter` or `gateway`), `baseURL`,
`decisionsBaseURL`, `defaultModel`, `allowedModels`, and `timeout` in the flow.
`apiKey` is declared as a native Node-RED **password credential** in both editor
and runtime. Configure a stable Node-RED `credentialSecret` for encrypted
credential storage. Flow exports omit the key; imports need separate credential
provisioning. No environment variable is changed or used in place of the key.

Timeout is an integer from 1 to 600000 milliseconds, default 60000. Allowed
models are exact IDs separated by commas or newlines. An omitted/blank model
selects `defaultModel`; a different ID must appear in `allowedModels`. There is
no model discovery or guarantee that an allowed model supports an operation.

Blank URLs use these defaults:

| Provider | Base URL | Decision URL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenRouter | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | `https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha` |
| AI Gateway | `https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v4/ai` | Same base URL |

Custom URLs require administrator approval in Node-RED `settings.js`:

```js
nodeRedAgentsModelProvider: {
  allowedBaseURLs: [
    "https://proxy.example/api/v1",
    "https://proxy.example/api/alpha",
  ],
},
```

Approval matches the complete normalized base URL, not just its hostname.
URLs require HTTPS and cannot contain user info, query strings, or fragments.
OpenRouter replaces a trailing `/v1` with `/alpha`; that derived custom URL
also requires approval. Other custom routes require an explicit approved
`decisionsBaseURL`. Gateway rejects that field. HTTP redirects are rejected.
Messages cannot override credentials or URLs; consumers must not pass arbitrary
message headers, provider options, or SDK options through to the SDK.

## Exact consumer API

Require `packages/node-red-agents/shared/model-provider.js` (relative to a
consumer node, usually `../../shared/model-provider`). Exports:

| Export | Signature and return |
| --- | --- |
| `getProviderConfig` | `(RED, id) => config` (synchronous; trusted internal access including `apiKey` and config lifetime `signal`) |
| `loadSDK` | `() => Promise<typeof import("ai")>` |
| `createProvider` | `(RED, id, options = {}) => Promise<adapter>`; `options.fetch` is an optional trusted transport/test seam |
| `sanitizeResult` | `(result, secrets = []) => plainResult` |
| `safeError` | `(error) => ModelProviderError` |

`getProviderConfig` throws `MISSING_PROVIDER_CONFIG`,
`MISSING_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL`, or `INVALID_PROVIDER_CONFIG`. Do not log or emit
its return value. The frozen adapter exposes:

- `sdk`, `provider`, `defaultModel`, `timeout` (no credential field).
- `createLanguageModel(requested?)`: synchronous language model instance.
- `createEmbeddingModel(requested?)`: synchronous embedding model instance.
- `createDecisionModel(requested?)`: synchronous v4 decision/evaluation model
  instance accepted by `sdk.experimental_decide`.
- `run(callback, { signal } = {}) => Promise<plainResult>`: callback receives
  `{ sdk, abortSignal, maxRetries: 0 }`. Pass these lifecycle options to the SDK.
- `sanitizeResult(result)`: credential-aware result projection.
- `safeError(error)`: sanitized error conversion.

```js
const { createProvider, safeError } = require("../../shared/model-provider");

// Resolve inside the request path so newly deployed credentials are used.
const adapter = await createProvider(RED, config.provider);
const result = await adapter.run(
  ({ sdk, ...lifecycle }) => sdk.generateText({
    model: adapter.createLanguageModel(),
    prompt: "Hello",
    ...lifecycle,
  }),
  { signal: controller.signal },
);
// Emit result, not raw SDK objects. Convert creation errors with safeError.
```

Use `sdk.embed({ model: adapter.createEmbeddingModel(id), value, ...lifecycle })`
for embedding, and `sdk.experimental_decide({ model:
adapter.createDecisionModel(id), state, questions, ...lifecycle })` for decisions.
Use model instances rather than SDK string model IDs (which resolve through the
global default provider). Do not mutate SDK globals or `process.env`.

Consumers own an AbortController for each active input and abort it on close.
The provider config node additionally aborts its lifetime signal on redeploy or
close: active runs cancel and old adapters reject subsequent runs. Timeout and
caller abort propagate to SDK fetch when lifecycle options are passed. `run`
also settles promptly if a callback ignores abort; it cannot stop arbitrary
callback side effects. Streaming results are outside this non-streaming API.

Safe results retain only `text`, `object`, `output`, `answers`, `rounding`,
`embedding`, `embeddings`, `usage`, `totalUsage`, `finishReason`, `warnings`,
`providerMetadata`, and `response`. Application payloads in `object`, `output`,
and `answers` preserve user-defined keys (including `token`, `password`, and
`body`). Metadata still removes nested auth/header/body/request/raw-response
fields. Known credential strings, URL-encoded credentials, and Bearer tokens
are redacted in both payloads and metadata, including object keys. Traversal
is depth-bounded and copies only own enumerable keys into plain data objects.
Model warnings, including streaming `stream-start` warnings, are sanitized
before SDK warning logging; `run` still returns non-streaming plain results. Use
`adapter.run` rather than logging raw model/SDK results or exceptions.

Errors have `name: "ModelProviderError"`, a fixed safe message, and a code:
`INVALID_PROVIDER_CONFIG`, `MISSING_PROVIDER_CONFIG`,
`MISSING_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL`, `REQUEST_TIMEOUT`, `REQUEST_ABORTED`,
`PROVIDER_AUTH` (401/403), `PROVIDER_RATE_LIMIT` (429), or `PROVIDER_ERROR`.
HTTP errors may include `statusCode`. Provider response bodies, original
messages, causes, and auth headers are not retained. Automatic retries are
disabled by the lifecycle options; downstream retry policies must be explicit.

# Model node

`model` makes direct AI SDK requests through a [model-provider](/docs/model-provider.md).
It uses the pinned AI SDK 7 contract and requires Node 22+. It does not spawn a
CLI, run tools, or select a fallback model.

## Configuration

| Field | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Provider | Required `model-provider` config node; credentials remain in its native Node-RED credential store. |
| Operation | `generate`, `structured`, or `embed`. |
| Model | Optional model ID; blank inherits the provider default. `msg.model` overrides this field. The provider enforces exact allowlisted IDs. |
| Input mode | `prompt` for text, `messages` for an array of text-only `{role, content}` objects. Supported roles: `system`, `user`, `assistant`. |
| Input | Typed Node-RED property, default `msg.payload`; supports `str`, `msg`, `flow`, `global`, `json`, `jsonata`. |
| JSON schema | Structured operation only: strict draft-07 object schema, validated with existing Ajv. Unknown keywords, invalid schemas and unresolved references fail before the request. |
| Timeout | `0` inherits the provider timeout; `1`–`600000` ms imposes an additional deadline. The earlier deadline wins. |
| Streaming | Generate or structured only; embedding requires one non-empty text value. |

Credentials, URLs, headers, provider options and arbitrary SDK options in messages
are not accepted as request overrides. Messages mode projects only `role` and
`content`; multimodal uploads and tool messages are outside this node's contract.
Messages mode opts into SDK 7's documented `allowSystemInMessages` option for both
generation and streaming, preserving system/user/assistant history order.

## Outputs

Output **1 (Final result)** sends exactly one successful message with
`msg.modelResult`. It preserves the original payload and unrelated fields.

- Generate: `text`, plus available `usage`, `totalUsage`, `finishReason`,
  `warnings`, `providerMetadata`.
- Structured: those generation fields plus schema-validated `object`. Uses
  `generateText`/`streamText` with `sdk.Output.object({schema: sdk.jsonSchema(...)})`
  and an Ajv validation callback, not hand-parsed provider text.
- Embed: `embedding` (numeric vector) and available SDK metadata. Uses `sdk.embed`
  with a provider-created embedding model. Batch embedding is not supported.

Metadata is projected and sanitized by the shared adapter. Raw SDK objects,
request headers and response bodies are not emitted.

Output **2 (Stream events)** sends preserved copies of the input with:

```json
{"modelEvent":{"type":"text-delta","text":"safe streamed text"}}
```

The node consumes the entire SDK `fullStream`, including error events, before
sending the final message. Text deltas are sanitized, with a retained suffix to
protect literal, URL-encoded, Base64 and JSON-escaped credentials split across chunks.
Buffering and final projection use the same shared encoding-variant policy.
Short responses may be buffered until
completion; long unfinished Bearer tokens are retained until their delimiter.
Stream-start warnings are sanitized before SDK warning logging. Partial events
can precede a failed request, but failure never produces a final success.

## Errors and lifecycle

Use a native Catch node scoped to the model node. Invalid input/schema errors
have code `INVALID_MODEL_INPUT` and fixed validation messages. Provider errors
use the shared sanitized error contract (`PROVIDER_AUTH`, `PROVIDER_RATE_LIMIT`,
`PROVIDER_ERROR`, configuration errors, `REQUEST_TIMEOUT`, `REQUEST_ABORTED`).
Unsupported provider/model features fail through Catch rather than fabricating a
result. Automatic retries are disabled.

Each input resolves the provider afresh and owns an independent AbortController.
Closing/redeploying aborts active requests and blocks late events/results.
Provider lifetime cancellation and its timeout remain authoritative; a node
timeout can shorten but cannot extend that timeout.

The S5 translation checks target the installed OpenCode **v2.0.28**. They do not

## Models and permissions

- CLI selectors use `provider/model#variant`. Model IDs can contain additional
  slashes, but neither the provider nor model ID can contain `#`.
- Explicit Effort replaces an embedded variant. Empty or repeated `#` suffixes
  fail validation instead of reaching the CLI.
- The v2 session-model endpoint takes
  `{ "model": { "providerID": "openai", "id": "gpt-5.2", "variant": "high" } }`.
  The variant is not part of `id`.
- Shared-provider authentication authorizes the base model, retaining the variant
  for OpenCode v2/auto selectors. Explicit v1 and Pi keep their literal model IDs.
- Permission rules use last-match precedence. Translation emits allows first,
  denies last, and maps `bash` to `shell`, `task` to `subagent`, and both `write`
  and `patch` to `edit`. This is not a strict allowlist: unspecified tools retain
  the upstream/default policy. Explicit v1 retains its existing tools-map behavior.

discarding provider response bodies and transport metadata. The existing

includes reasoning; do not add reasoning again when deriving its total.

# OpenCode v2 server turn completion

`agent-server` supplies a stable caller-generated `msg_`-prefixed `id` to
`POST /api/session/{sessionID}/prompt` and correlates it with the projected transcript from
`GET /api/session/{sessionID}/message`. This behavior is specific to v2; the v1
synchronous message path is unchanged.

## Terminal contract

The v2.0.28 transcript is newest first. In chronological order, the admitted
user message anchors the turn and the first subsequent `type: "idle"` message
bounds its execution. Older idle markers and messages after that terminal
boundary do not belong to the turn. An assistant's `time.completed` marks a
step, including tool-call steps; it does not establish execution completion.

- `succeeded`: return the last completed assistant message inside the turn.
  Its text parts become the result payload; an empty answer is permitted.
- `failed`: reject, using a fixed, sanitized error label when a structured
  terminal error is present. Do not return partial assistant text.
- `interrupted`: reject as `MessageAbortedError: message aborted`, even if a
  preceding assistant step completed.

Missing user anchors or terminal markers keep polling within the existing
request deadline. Invalid terminal outcomes and successful turns without a
completed assistant reject rather than manufacture success. Once a terminal
failure or interruption is observed, later transcript updates cannot turn
that operation into success.

The node retains its existing `completed`/`failed` lifecycle events. Completion
polling follows opaque `cursor.next` values until the admitted anchor is visible,
including turns longer than the default 50-message page. History fetches traverse
the complete newest-first transcript. Each traversal shares one deadline across
pages and response bodies; repeated or malformed cursors fail explicitly. An empty
page terminates traversal even if the preceding page supplied a non-null cursor
(verified against v2.0.28).

## Uncertain submission and timeout recovery

The request deadline covers agent/model selection, admission, completion polling,
and response-body consumption, not only response headers. A failed admission
request may have committed remotely. Its caller-generated ID remains the recovery
anchor even when no admission response arrives; the node does not retry submission
or accept a mismatched response ID.

After a submitted turn fails, the node retains its local busy reservation while
interrupting execution and confirming a durable idle marker for that same anchor.
Recovery has a separate shared budget of the smaller of the request timeout and
five seconds. Confirmed success, failure, or interruption permits reuse, but never
converts the original failed request into a result or `completed` event. An interrupt
acknowledgement without a correlated idle is insufficient.

If interrupt fails or idle cannot be verified, the node removes and stops its owned
private daemon. Reusing the removed session ID is rejected; omitting the ID starts
a replacement daemon. Process shutdown uses the existing bounded SIGTERM/SIGKILL
cleanup. Network and HTTP diagnostics for v2 discard arbitrary remote error bodies.
Cleanup succeeds only after a confirmed child exit; exceeding its confirmation
deadline reports failure rather than claiming termination succeeded.

## Lifecycle and compatibility safeguards

Concurrent inputs reserve startup slots before asynchronous port allocation, so
starting daemons count against `maxInstances`. Spawn errors fail the input without
an unhandled child-process error. Unexpected idle-daemon exits retire the session
and emit a fixed safe failure; in-flight requests report their own failure once.

Automatic CLI version probes have a three-second timeout and bounded output.
Only successful detection is cached; a failed probe warns and temporarily falls
back to v1, allowing later requests to detect v2. Explicit version selection
continues to bypass detection.

V2 private daemons receive canonical `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` matching the client's
Basic Auth password, overriding any inherited canonical password. The v1-compatible
server-password alias is also supplied, but v2.0.28 prioritizes the canonical key.

Unlike v1, v2.0.28 `run --session` explicitly creates unknown session IDs. The
`agent` adapter therefore checks existence using `opencode api --standalone GET
/api/session/{sessionID}` before resuming. A failed check produces a fixed error
and never submits the prompt. The positional-argument-only shell guard then
`exec`s the run CLI, retaining the runtime's owned process group, SIGINT policy,
cwd/PWD, environment and timeout. This guard requires a POSIX `sh`; it never uses
the shared background service. Checking and running use successive private servers;
external deletion between those operations is not an atomic compare-and-resume.

Manual CLI cancellation is non-retryable, including when `retryOnError` is `all`;
timeouts retain their retry policy. Cancellation snapshots owned descendants before
interrupting. After the leader exits, group escalation requires an identity-verified
surviving member of that original group; other verified descendants are signalled
individually, never by an unverified detached group ID. Linux identity uses
`/proc/<pid>/stat` start ticks; other POSIX systems use second-resolution `ps lstart`,
which cannot distinguish same-second PID reuse. Snapshot-to-signal races remain
possible without kernel process handles, and descendants spawned or reparented
before the ownership snapshot may escape discovery. Inspection failures are reported
in execution diagnostics rather than permitting unverified post-exit group signals.

## Contract evidence and validation

Sources: [official v2 API](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/api) and
